mission_07: Custom AI accelerators are designed specifically for neural network workloads, with systolic arrays as the core compute engine. Each Processing Element (PE) performs a multiply-accumulate (MAC) operation, and the systolic dataflow feeds weights and activations through the array in a wavefront pattern. The roofline model characterizes performance as the minimum of compute-bound and memory-bound throughput. In this mission, you implement individual PEs with MAC accumulators, a 2D systolic array accelerator that loads weights and computes matrix products, cycle counting for systolic dataflow, MAC utilization efficiency, and a benchmark framework that compares different accelerator architectures using the roofline model to determine whether workloads are compute-bound or memory-bound.
